answer: Batch-correlated enclave seats: admission needs a remote attestation from a distinct secure chip, and a registry binds each endorsement key to one seat. First boot seals a crystal nonce inside the chip, so a cloned image carries a duplicate and both void. Chips ship in certified batches; if two seats from one batch are proven kin, a beacon-drawn raven voids every seat in that batch and the bond held in the vault is forfeit. A k-farm must source k chips across many batches at climbing marginal prices, so correlated loss makes cost super-linear in k.
